title: DHCP Pool Configuration

steps.teachingPoint: DHCP is like a receptionist handing out visitor badges - devices get IP addresses automatically instead of picking their own!
Without DHCP, you'd have to manually type an IP on every computer, phone, and tablet. Imagine doing that for 500 devices!
G0/1 is our LAN interface where DHCP clients connect - computers, phones, printers, and more.
This IP becomes the 'default gateway' - the exit door for all traffic leaving your network!
Just like a light switch - you need to turn it ON for it to work!

steps.objective: Exclude addresses for the router and servers
steps.teachingPoint: Some IPs should NEVER be given out - the router, servers, printers. We 'exclude' .1 through .10 to reserve them!

steps.objective: Create a DHCP pool named SCHOOL_NETWORK
steps.teachingPoint: A 'pool' is like a bucket of addresses. Think of it like school lockers - students don't pick their own, they get assigned one!
This tells DHCP which subnet to use. Combined with exclusions, clients get .11 through .254
The gateway is the 'exit door' - this must match the IP we put on G0/1!
DNS translates website names to IPs. 8.8.8.8 is Google's free DNS server.
Look for 'ip dhcp pool SCHOOL_NETWORK' and the excluded-address line in the config!
Done! Devices on G0/1 will now automatically get IPs from .11-.254 with gateway .1 and DNS 8.8.8.8

assertions.description: Configuration must be saved with 'write memory'

legacyCommands: ! KEY CONCEPTS FOR MIDDLE SCHOOLERS
! THE DORA HANDSHAKE (How devices get an IP):
! D = Discover (device: 'Anyone have an IP for me?')
! O = Offer (router: 'Here's 192.168.100.50!')
! R = Request (device: 'I'll take that one!')
! A = Acknowledge (router: 'Done! It's yours for 24 hours.')
! Q: Why do we EXCLUDE addresses?
! A: So the router doesn't accidentally give away its own IP,
!    or addresses we want for servers and printers!
! Q: What is a 'lease'?
! A: DHCP addresses are temporary - like checking out a library
!    book. After the lease expires, the device asks for renewal.
! Q: What's the difference between STATIC and DHCP?
! A: Static = you type the IP yourself (permanent)
!    DHCP = the router gives you an IP automatically (temporary)
! WHAT EACH COMMAND MEANS
! ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.100.1 192.168.100.10
!   ^ Reserves .1 through .10 (won't be given to clients)
! ip dhcp pool SCHOOL_NETWORK
!   ^ Creates a pool - name can be anything meaningful
!   ^ The subnet to assign addresses FROM
! default-router 192.168.100.1
!   ^ The gateway IP clients will use (our router's LAN IP)
! dns-server 8.8.8.8
!   ^ Where clients look up website names (Google's DNS)
